I can attest 100% that hospitals are on the same parallel as extended care facilities/nursing homes. I am an "old-school" nurse who is 100% cognizant and knowledgeable about nursing care delivery, whether it is hospital or nursing home based. Radical changes in the delivery of patient care have occurred nationwide in a relatively short period of time.

Finding nursing staff, whether it be the nurse or the aide, who actually delivers total/complete nursing care is hard to find. I am not necessarily referring to the patient care provided in the critical care units, such as intensive care; step-down; or other highly-specialized areas. I am referring to your basic adult medical or surgical floor, where the patient is still acutely ill but not in need of 1:1 or 2:1 care and monitoring.

The reasons for decline have occurred for several reasons. First of all, it didn't occur suddenly. It was an accumulative process, and once this process started, layer upon layer upon layer of health care facility changes have occurred under the facade of improving patient care even if a hospital or nursing home had nothing wrong with it in the first place. Good hospitals or nursing homes gradually turned into poor ones, and the bad ones either stayed the same or became worse.

There are 2 entities to blame - the government and the government. One makes or breaks a hospital/nursing home and the other makes or breaks the licensing boards, particularly the licensing boards for nurses. For the past several years, the makes have been on a downward spiral.
